The good: Mechanics are improved and refined over the previous entries in the Borderlands franchise.

The bad: The characters, particularly the main antagonists, are unimaginably awful.  This game is overloaded with voice acting and most of it unlistenable.

The ugly: My game is currently softlocked because of a bug that has existed since at least 2020.  I am stuck on Mount Maraboshi in the Legend of McSmugger DLC mission.  I cannot collect the three MacGuffins necessary to proceed.  I cannot get the boss to summon.  I cannot GET DOWN OFF THE MOUNTAIN.  Many searches for fixes later, it appears as if the only reliable option is using a savegame editor.  This is insane.

I cannot recommend this game in its current state.  If and when I get a working fix (and maybe complete the game), I'll update my review.  Don't hold your breath.

Borderlands 3 is like buying yourself a delicious cake with the exact type of amazingly fluffy, homemade cake mix you've been craving for weeks but you bite into it to find it's glazed in really, really gross icing. I cannot stress how good the actual cake is but you should just be aware that you'll have to either stomach the icing or shave it off. 

BL3 has such an amazing diversity in weapons and gear and it is visually breathtaking at times but the story and dialogue (ESPECIALLY THE DIALOGUE) absolutely get in the way of the pacing and brings down the overall quality of the game. The DLC's for this game feel like complementary cupcakes you buy along with your cake and you'll probably end up liking them more than the cake itself. 

I really love this game; I have 300+ hours clocked in between Steam and Epic Games. I absolutely believe that Borderlands 2 is the better experience in its entirety but I believe that 3 is the better GAME. I might just be hungry but I'll go back to explaining it in terms of cake: Borderlands 2 has both really good cake mix and icing but borderlands 3 has much better cake mix but detestable icing. For real man, that BL3 icing is bad enough that it tricks you into thinking the the batter with sprinkles, layers and chocolate chunks is bad too. Your enjoyment of this game is going to be determined by how much you value good icing and how willing you are to buy a cake knowing the icing sucks balls.

I'm going to go purchase a cake now. Bazinga!

With the amount of time I have put into this game, I have sort of gotten over how brazenly annoying the main story is. The plotline itself isn't total hog's wash, it is simply that much of the humor is dated and soul wrenching to hear said out loud. Ava is an annoying little creature that should be disposed of, but that was probably the point, so I don't loathe the character. Claptrap, as always, should be scrapped and repurposed as sewer line so at least the ♥♥♥♥ coming out of it is out of my sight. It is far from the worst story I've ever sat through, but it could have been much better.

Buuuuuuut the DLCs have rather good stories that I actually liked playing through multiple times. Even when 100%ing the game I found the stories to be perfectly good. So why couldn't they just have done a different main story? Not sure. There are a bunch of parts of the main story that I could see placed into a different plotline that would both be more interesting and less miserable to sit through.

Speaking of 100% achievements, who at gearbox though some of these achievements were okay? Watch deathtrap kill 50 enemies? I like to think that a good achievement design would be one that is difficult in some manner and that takes an amount of skill. This neither takes skill nor is difficult. It takes sitting on your ass for a several minutes watching an npc waddle up to enemies and melee them and hit them with an electric attack that doesn't stun long enough to close any sort of gap. Truly astounding. I also love the one for extracting 100 items from arms race that only counts for the host, so me and my friend I 100% games with had to extract a total of 200 items which took aprox. way to long. Why 100? Why not 50? Hell, why not one for extracting an amount of legendaries? No idea. The numbers on a few of the achievements are a tad over tuned. Like the one for getting 50 mysterious eridium piles, because why on earth would you ever use that artifact or use it for long enough to get 50 naturally without knowing about the achievement. But these are all far less obtuse than some of BL2's so I wont complain too much.

Slight nit pick, put I'm not the biggest fan of legendaries being the only useful rarity outside of some edge cases/quest given items. Having some variety is nice, but i will say that being able to auto scrap epics and lower without regard is kinda nice.

Cuarta entrega de la saga Borderlands de la mano de los chicos de Gearbox, como siempre agregando mecánicas y Buscacámaras nuevos.

En este caso, Borderlands 3 nos lleva a la búsqueda de Cámaras a lo largo de la galaxia, teniendo localizaciones en múltiples zonas del espacio (en contraste con los anteriores Borderlands, los cuales tenían una única localización). Esto añade variedad a la cantidad de ecosistemas que nos podemos llegar a encontrar a lo largo de nuestra aventura, variando la flora y fauna de dichos parajes.

La historia transcurre unos años después de los acontecimientos acaecidos en Borderlands 2 y Tales from the Borderlands, la cual se centra en la búsqueda del mapa de la Gran Cámara. Una vez tomemos control de nuestro personaje (excepto la Sirena, el resto son clases nuevas como el Domabestias, la Artillera, y el Operativo) nos uniremos a la fuerzas de los Invasores Carmesíes (liderados por Lilith, una de las protagonistas del Borderlands original) para investigar a Los Hijos de la Cámara y sus líderes (Tyreen y Troy Calypso), una secta que está buscando los fragmentos del mapa para hacerse con el control de la galaxia.

Tras realizar las primeras misiones en la que se nos explica la jugabilidad a modo de tutorial, nos meteremos en faena viajando por la galaxia en la nave Sanctuary III, que será nuestra base de operaciones y punto de enlace con cualquier localización del juego.

Lo primero que me llama la atención es la GRAN mejora gráfica que ha experimentado la franquicia (Borderlands 2 y Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel tienen el mismo motor con prácticamente lo mismo), recreando tanto los modelos de todos los personajes (ya sean nuevos o que repitan presencia de otras entregas) como de los objetos con los que puedes interactuar (barriles, contenedores, armas, munición, etc.). Esto da una sensación de gran avance hacia delante, ya que la saga se estaba quedando estancada a nivel visual. Aparte, el personaje jugable que elijas aparece en la pantalla y da sensación de que realmente lo controlamos (si giras la cámara hacia abajo, verás las piernas, o si corres, verás los brazos agitándose); son detalles, pero para mí son importantes ya que hacen más inmersiva la experiencia desde mi punto de vista.

Las melodías son espectaculares (maravilloso el tema de la Bola de Katagawa, Supernova Dreamsicle), y han dejado de reutilizar los mismos efectos de sonido que se llevan escuchando desde el primer Borderlands. El doblaje al castellano también es muy bueno (no hay necesidad de cambiarlo al inglés debido a un nefasto trabajo por parte de los actores).

El control es el MEJOR de cualquier entrega de la saga hasta la fecha, estando pulido el control al límite. Han agregado movimientos nuevos como colgarse de muros tras saltar (como en el DOOM) o hacer deslizamientos tras correr (pudiendo disparar sin problema cual héroe de acción clásico). El juego es mucho más frenético que en las entregas anteriores, dando vida a variedad infinita de cómo afrontar un asalto de enemigos o un combate contra un boss.

En cuanto a la potenciación de nuestro personaje, tendrá un total de 3 árboles de habilidades (4 si posees el DLC Designer's Cut) con habilidades ÚNICAS por cada árbol, pudiendo alterar la potencia y efectos equipando las habilidades desbloqueadas. Esto añade más variedad aún si cabe a como desarrollar a nuestro personaje en función de nuestras necesidades o gustos, siendo un puntazo muy bueno.

El juego tiene una duración alta, necesitando en torno a 40 horas para terminar la historia principal si sólo nos centamos en ello; hay una buena cantidad de misiones secundarias, arenas de batalla, y contenido post-game que nos permite alargar casi x5 la duración en caso de querer seguir jugando. Y para rematar la faena, hay 6 DLCs de contenido, siendo 4 de ellos magistrales trayendo de vuelta a viejos conocidos de la franquicia y expandiendo el lore de dichos personajes y de la saga.

Sólo he encontrado un par de peros:
- La historia: por bien que suene el resumen inicial que hice, es bastante flojita en varios puntos, aunque luego recupere de cara al final. Aún así, es la peor narrativa de toda la franquicia hasta el momento.
- Diversos problemas de sincronización con Steam y con Shift (herramienta incluida en el juego de cara al multijugador cross-plataforma). Esto se soluciona arrancando Steam en modo Administrador, y modificando algunos parámetros en el juego, pero no es intuitivo y es necesario buscar esa información en el foro del juego en Steam. Si no haces esto, cada X tiempo aparecen molestos pop-ups que pausan el juego hasta que no los cierres (si es en multijugador es aún peor puesto que al pausar y acceder a un menú el tiempo NO se detiene).

En definitiva, el mejor Borderlands de la saga a nivel jugable. Si bien es cierto que a nivel narrativo es muy flojo, no por ello es menos disfrutable (lo dice un fanático de la saga). Muy recomendado.

Berikut adalah review mendalam untuk game Borderlands pertama yang mengusung genre looter-shooter ikonik, dengan skor 8.2 / 10.

Review: Borderlands – Kekacauan Penuh Warna dan Gairah Menjarah yang Adiktif
Sejak dirilis pertama kali oleh Gearbox Software, Borderlands berani mengambil perjudian besar dengan menggabungkan dua genre yang sangat berbeda: sudut pandang First-Person Shooter (FPS) yang cepat dengan sistem mekanik Role-Playing Game (RPG) pengumpul jarahan (loot) ala Diablo. Hasilnya adalah sebuah formula unik yang melahirkan sub-genre baru dan mendefinisikan ulang arti kepuasan dalam bermain game kooperatif.

1. Presentasi dan Gaya Visual: Seni Sel-Shading yang Menawan (8.5/10)
Keputusan Gearbox mengubah gaya visual Borderlands dari realistis menjadi cel-shaded komik di menit-menit akhir pengembangan adalah sebuah berkah tersembunyi. Dunia Pandora tampil dengan estetika pasca-apokaliptik yang gersang, penuh debu, karat, dan gurun pasir, namun tetap terasa hidup berkat palet warna yang cerah dan garis tepi tebal ala buku komik. Desain makhluk mutan, bandit psikopat, hingga berbagai variasi senjata memiliki ciri khas kuat yang membuat mata tidak mudah bosan menjelajahi planet Pandora.

2. Gameplay dan Sistem Loot: Adiktif dan Memuaskan (8.5/10)
Inti dari Borderlands terletak pada siklus pertempuran dan perburuan senjatanya. Dengan slogan "87 gazillion guns", game ini memang benar-benar menawarkan variasi senjata yang hampir tak terbatas berkat sistem pembuatan prosedur acak (procedural generation).

Setiap senjata memiliki pabrikan (manufacturer) masing-masing dengan karakteristik unik—ada yang fokus pada akurasi tinggi, ada yang memicu efek elemen pembakar/asam, hingga peluru yang bisa memantul.

Sistem kelas keempat Vault Hunter (Mordecai, Lilith, Roland, dan Brick) menawarkan gaya bermain yang berbeda drastis, mulai dari penyergapan jarak jauh, kekuatan elemen teleportasi, pertahanan taktis, hingga amukan jarak dekat yang beringas.

Namun, sistem inventaris di seri pertama ini terkadang terasa kaku dan manajemen item bisa menjadi pekerjaan rumah yang melelahkan menjelang pertengahan permainan.

3. Cerita, Dunia, dan Atmosfer (7.5/10)
Planet Pandora digambarkan sebagai planet perbatasan antariksa yang liar, dipenuhi oleh perusahaan korporat kejam, bandit gila, dan mitos tentang harta karun alien misterius bernama The Vault.

Meskipun fondasi dunianya sangat menarik, narasi utama di game pertamanya tergolong cukup tipis. Sebagian besar cerita disampaikan melalui teks misi atau hologram, alih-alih interaksi sinematik yang mendalam. Meski demikian, kepribadian karakter, humor satir yang kelam, dan kehadiran robot ceriwis Claptrap berhasil menyelamatkan atmosfer permainan sehingga tetap terasa seru dan jenaka.

4. Desain Misi dan Mode Multiplayer (8.0/10)
Borderlands dirancang untuk dinikmati bersama teman (kooperatif hingga 4 pemain). Bermain secara co-op mengubah dinamika permainan menjadi jauh lebih kacau dan menyenangkan, di mana kombinasi kemampuan kelas yang tepat dapat melibas musuh-musuh elit dengan mudah.

Sayangnya, beberapa struktur misi utama di paruh kedua game terasa repetitif—seringkali pemain disuruh bolak-balik mengambil barang atau membersihkan area (fetch quest). Perjalanan yang cukup panjang tanpa kendaraan yang bervariasi di awal juga sempat terasa sedikit membosankan.

Kesimpulan: Skor 8.2 / 10
Borderlands adalah sebuah pionir yang berhasil memadukan adrenalin tembak-menembak dengan obsesi mengumpulkan senjata terbaik. Meskipun memiliki beberapa kekurangan pada variasi misi dan sistem narasi yang minimalis di awal, adiksi untuk mendapatkan senjata legendaris berikutnya membuat pemain terus kembali ke tanah Pandora. Game ini wajib dicatat sebagai salah satu fondasi terbaik bagi para pecinta game aksi kooperatif.

Borderlands 3 is a tactical shooter... with tactical BB guns in the hands of a drunk character, in a universe of bad jokes and poor city planners who never quite worked out what a street is for by the time they got to the space age.

It loads slow. Frequently has massive freezes, pauses, or frame rate dips on *great* hardware for the specs of this game. The sound design is genuinely awful, with key dialog being drowned out by every other sound in the game as characters alternate between normal voices and whispers in the same cinematics. The character controls, for lack of a better word, are both sloshy and slow at the same time. And there's not one grenade in the game that works like a grenade...
And if you're thinking about the gunplay? Forget about it. You're going to take the most twitchy, physics-less animations on your enemies, tiny hitboxes for critical spots, combine that with *minimal* boosts to damage for hitting those critical spots, and pair it with what feels like BB guns or paintball guns going up against armored foes and tanks for the damage they do and the stun effects they have on an enemy hit.

This is cartoon Borderlands. And Borderlands as a franchise was already a cartoon of a serious shooter game, fun most of the time but a little fast and loose with what it was doing. This is a meme of a meme, and it's lost its roots.

I've given it as much time as I could tolerate at the time of this posting. Trying numerous characters, trying to push through the first couple of planets, trying different builds, and trying to find some gun, some frame rate fix, some control setting that would let me enjoy this game. It's just a bad game in the series, and so at 69 hours gameplay, I'm leaving that review.

Borderlands 3 is proof that Gearbox learned exactly one lesson from the last decade: if the guns feel good enough, players will forgive almost anything, including a script that thinks it's funnier than it is.

And to be fair, the gunplay does feel good — genuinely, mechanically good. Sliding into cover, dual-wielding a corrosive shotgun and a fire pistol, watching numbers explode off an enemy's head in six different colors — that's the hook, and it works. The RPG systems here arguably outclass most other shared-world shooters, and the skill trees give you enough room to actually build a character instead of just picking a class and pulling triggers. 
techradar

Everything else is the game daring you to keep liking it. The writing is Telltale-tier quippy dialogue that mistakes volume for wit — every NPC talks like they're auditioning for a podcast. Vehicles and vehicular combat are too imprecise to be more than a novelty, so you end up walking past the "new movement mechanic" they were so proud of. And then there's the endgame, which is where this thing really falls apart: Anointed enemies — teleporting, high-defense mini-bosses that need a second execution kill after you've already killed them once — turn Mayhem-tier difficulty into a war of attrition against bullet sponges rather than a skill check. It's the kind of difficulty scaling that mistakes "enemy has more HP" for "encounter is more interesting." 

The loot chase is the actual product here, and Gearbox knows it — legendaries flood in fast enough early on that they stop feeling legendary, then the game slams the brakes and makes you grind Mayhem levels for the stuff that matters. Classic live-service pacing: give away the dopamine for free, then paywall it behind time instead of money.

If you love looter-shooters and have three friends to split the tedium with, it's fine — genuinely fun in short co-op bursts where nobody has time to notice the writing. Solo, going for 100%, it overstays its welcome by about fifteen hours. Wait for a deep sale, and skip anything that requires you to read a subtitle to understand a joke.

Idgaf about the potty humor or ♥♥♥♥♥♥ jokes. That has always been in the borderlands series. 

The UI and animation has been completely "modernized". The simplicity is what helped make it attractive. 

They even messed up the cell shading. In previous entries it was hard lines with duller colors. Now its all bright colors and unnecessary details to make the world feel more "hardcore". 

The animations have been way overcooked. Lots of exaggerated movements just to show "look how much cooler this is and how much work we put into it!" When in reality it just makes aiming less fun and more annoying to look at.

Even the "big bad" made himself known in BL2 by now. In 3 its just a name with a face. You have no emotional attachment to any of the characters as they were before or the bad guy. 

The quests are also now WAY more spread out. In 1 and 2 there were "quests hubs" where you would go to get the majority of your side quests. Now you have to do a lot of running around. It more of feels like this was done to add time padding to the game to make you play longer and please shareholders.

They somehow made claptrap even more obnoxious. In 1 and 2 he was just a humorous loser. Now in 3 he's just pathetic.

The only thing left compared to previous entries are the older characters, quality loot system, cell animation and Pandora.

Although the live action lilith, as she appeared in BL2, is the same actor. They made the camera quality WAY too good. Its super off putting. Overall she doesn't look that bad. But compared to the previous enteries. The telepathic (live action) version of the sirens talking to you were always super grainy and missing a lot of detail. This isn't the case in BL3. Its just way too good quality and completely breaks immersion compared to the cartoony nature of the game.

I should have paid more attention to the hours played so I could get a refund. The only way I'll even attempt BL4 is if it is given to me for free. If you absolutely must buy this game. Borderlands 3 is yet another solid entry in the franchise. It's exactly what you'd expect from a Borderlands game, but reworked and improved in all the right ways.

[b]First, I'll start with the POSITIVES:[/b]
+ The looter-shooter gameplay is absolute crack. The loop goes: find an overpowered gun → use it until it becomes average → replace it with an even better gun → repeat. It's an endless cycle of chasing the next OP weapon, and the gameplay loop is honestly near perfect.
+ The gameplay itself is top-tier. Between the skill trees, player progression, huge variety of enemies, and endless weapons, the game stayed fresh almost all the way to the end.
+ No complaints about performance. I didn't experience any crashes, bugs, or noticeable glitches. It was a super smooth experience.
+ There's a solid 30 hours of content just in the main game, and probably closer to 40 if you take your time and complete the side stuff
+ It's a great "turn your brain off" shooter. You can relax and just enjoy blasting through enemies for most of the game. (This could be a negative for some people, but it's exactly what I was looking for.)

[b]Here are some NEGATIVES that come to mind:[/b]
- The story is pretty dumb. I'm still not sure how I feel about the main villains being an influencer/streamer duo.
- Some of the map design is a chore. It feels like certain areas were made unnecessarily huge just to pad the game's length.
- Sanctuary is awful to navigate. Why does it have three floors with almost no cohesive flow between them?
- The Borderlands humor and overall atmosphere didn't feel as fresh this time around. I miss when most of the characters were just completely insane. It felt more tame.

Overall, I'd give Borderlands 3 a 3.5/5. The gameplay loop is what will always keep me coming back to this series. I got exactly what I wanted from Borderlands, and even a little more.

I cheated myself on BL3. I picked this game up after bouncing off of BL2 multiple times, and I should've known better.

To their credit, BL3 improves on BL2:
- Gameplay feels less clunky and fatiguing right from the start.

But, I still felt, hours in, that it had no staying power with me because of the same pain points:
- The wacky, cringe, unserious and wild writing doesn't land for me, including the characters. I'm not really compelled.
- The world design just feels... monotonous, disinteresting, unmemorable. It all just blurred together in a way that made it meaningless to me.

BL3 was a good lesson - I gave BL2 a fair shake and didn't love it, and I should've done my due diligence to know that BL3 did not set out to change and capture a player like me. 

Borderlands - not just 3, but the franchise, is not for me - but it deserves the cornerstone status it has in paving the way for the looter-shooter genre and capturing a lot of players with it's wacky delivery and iconic art style. Even if I don't enjoy it, I respect it.
